title: AiON
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Recently orphaned high-schooler Tatsuya Tsugawa, left a fortune and his father's last words to become 'a man of great vessel', tries to help Seine, a cold girl others bully (AniList; MangaUpdates). Seine is immortal and hunts parasitic sea creatures that control humans and push them to hateful acts, using a beast called AiON; the Comic Book Bin review describes her struggle as against mermaids. An 11-volume supernatural drama.
life_message: It holds up kindness and steadfast help toward someone others reject, even at personal cost.

content.note: Violent struggle with sea creatures (review); MangaUpdates Blood and Gore, Attempted Murder, Revenge.
Reviewer calls the art 'creepy at times'; mind-controlling parasites (AniList summary).
Childhood love and romance (MangaUpdates); friends call Seine a 'masochist pervert' (AniList summary).
Grief after parents' death; both leads bullied (review; summaries).

dominant: Compassion for the outcast, honoring a father's wish, immortality

frames.aligns: Tatsuya's mercy toward a bullied, rejected girl.

frames.concerns: Demonic-like parasites and immortality outside God.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Being 'a man of great vessel' is a personal standard, not a feud (AniList).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Tatsuya acts on conscience against friends' advice (AniList).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Father's wish guides him, but he helps a stranger (summaries).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Peers at school; guardians and foster parents (MangaUpdates).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Fairy-tale folklore in a modern school (MangaUpdates).

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese school bullying (ijime) and a father's dying wish as a binding obligation on a son.
